premise_being_tested: The premise is no longer about which product to build. Four of the six checked options have now been refuted by outside evidence and all four failed on the same term: nothing reached a first buyer unattended. In every near-success on record the first buyer arrived because a third party with reach posted about the thing — an X account for PredictionJobs, Hacker News sending more real users in three hours than three months of search did for Stripe Fee Auditor, Product Hunt for Nomad List, Stack Overflow answers for IPinfo. Google's own Search Essentials says meeting the requirements does not guarantee crawl, index or display, and lists telling relevant communities as a basic step. So the premise now under test is the constraint, not the product: 'no recurring owner actions' was what excluded the only route with a buyer behind it, and it excluded it on a cost — repeated posting — that the evidence for that route does not contain. That is what lap 3 corrected and what task .i is aimed at breaking. If you disagree, say so and survey #1 instead — but disagree on purpose.
